title: Make String a Subsequence Using Cyclic Increments
summary: Given two strings str1 and str2, determine if str2 can be made a subsequence of str1 by performing at most one operation where each selected character in str1 is incremented cyclically to the next character.
statement: Given two strings str1 and str2, determine if str2 can be made a subsequence of str1 by performing at most one operation where each selected character in str1 is incremented cyclically to the next character. Return true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: Both strings are nonempty lowercase strings.
In one operation, any selected source characters advance once, with z wrapping to a.
Return whether str2 can become a subsequence after at most one such simultaneous operation.
hints: Each source character can match either itself or its single cyclic successor.
Greedily match the earliest still-needed target character while scanning the source once.
Advance the target pointer whenever the current source character or its successor equals the target character.
Using the earliest possible source position never removes a future option and leaves the longest suffix for remaining target characters, proving the subsequence greedy choice.
editorial: Using the earliest possible source position never removes a future option and leaves the longest suffix for remaining target characters, proving the subsequence greedy choice.

tests.explanation: Keep a and advance c to d, producing the target as a subsequence.
Advance z to a and c to d, using both selected indices in the one operation.
